concerns.text: The plan proposes calculating Pearson correlation between aggregated SHAP importance and a vector of 10+ independent descriptors (Hammett, Taft, etc.). However, the plan does not specify how these external descriptors (e.g., Taft Es, Verloop B1) are computed for the specific dataset molecules. Without a defined method to generate these ground-truth descriptors for every reaction in the dataset, the 'construct validity' of the correlation test is broken; you cannot correlate model features against a vector that is not actually constructed.

The plan acknowledges a power limitation for N < 500 but fails to define a minimum viable sample size for the specific statistical tests proposed (bootstrap CI, permutation tests). For a regression task with high variance (chemical kinetics), a sample size of 500 may be statistically underpowered to detect the effect size required to claim 'significant improvement' (SC-002) or 'significant correlation' (SC-003) with p < 0.05. The plan needs a formal power analysis or a justification for the chosen N based on expected effect sizes in chemical ML literature.

The normalization strategy (FR-001) relies on imputing missing Activation Energy (Ea) with a 'reaction-class-specific average'. This introduces a systematic confound: the normalized rate constant (k_298) will be artificially correlated with the imputation class, potentially creating a spurious signal that the GNN learns instead of true electronic effects. The plan does not propose a sensitivity analysis to determine if this imputation noise overwhelms the signal, threatening the causal validity of the learned features.
